newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTZ-CRA defends Freeport record in Indonesia.
newsitem.headline: RTZ-CRA defends Freeport record in Indonesia.

text.p: Global miner RTZ-CRA on Wednesday defended its partner in Indonesia's Grasberg copper and gold mine against claims of human rights abuses, but acknowledged concerns over unrest there.
RTZ-CRA deputy chairman John Uhrig told the company's annual meeting in Melbourne that he had visited the Grasberg project last year to assess the operation for himself.

Facing a barrage of questions over recent unrest around the mine in remote Irian Jaya province, Uhrig denied the mine's 86 percent owner and operator, Freeport McMoRan Copper and Gold Inc, was involved in rights abuses.

"CRA is satisfied that Freeport and PT Freeport Indonesia not only respect human rights but also operate to internationally acceptable environmental and community standards ...," Uhrig told shareholders.
PT Freeport Indonesia Co is a Freeport subsidiary.
After the meeting, Uhrig told reporters that some Indonesian police had been housed within Freeport's mine complex and that he understood the company wanted to end this arrangement.
"It is true that at one stage the police were accommodated in a building that was part of Freeport's infrastructure," he said.
"That still existed at the time I visited there last year and it's my understanding that there was likely to be a change," Uhrig said.
RTZ-CRA's London annual meeting, held two weeks ago, also drew criticism over Freeport's Grasberg operation.
Lobby group World Development Movement is campaigning for RTZ-CRA to withdraw its investment in the huge open cut mine.
RTZ-CRA is a dual listed entity with RTZ shares traded in London and CRA shares traded on the Australian Stock Exchange.
